answer: Behavioral drift scoring names the mechanism. Each identity builds a baseline of timing, tool use, and phrasing; similarity of drift patterns across identities is measured against a reef of historical norms, and clusters exceeding a set correlation are flagged after the fact. Flagged identities must pass a costly re-attestation fable of randomized tasks before regaining standing, so a sybil farm’s shared habits betray it while honest users rarely trigger the wharf of review. The attacker pays per-identity retraining and re-attestation, scaling cost linearly with farm size.
